proposals.before: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (12 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (9 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
proposals.reason: Yuanyan 1 is 12 BCE, so Yuanyan 4 is 9 BCE; the parenthetical Western year is wrong.

proposals.before: He enfeoffed his maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis of Yang'an, and Ding Ming's son Man as Marquis of Pingzhou.
proposals.after: He enfeoffed his maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis of Yang'an, and his maternal uncle's son Man as Marquis of Pingzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 舅子滿 means son of a maternal uncle, not specifically Ding Ming's son; s0036 names Man's father as Zhong (忠), a different (deceased) uncle.

proposals.before: In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Previously I commanded Xia Heliang and others to propose changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.
proposals.after: In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others proposed changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.
proposals.reason: 時詔/侍詔 is the office title Attendant-at-edict (as correctly rendered in s0139), not a verb meaning the emperor commanded them.

proposals.before: In the eighth month, an edict stated: 'At the time I ordered Xia Helang and others to propose changing the era name and designation, increasing the water clock periods, believing it could permanently secure the state.
proposals.after: In the eighth month, an edict stated: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Helang and others proposed changing the era name and designation, increasing the water clock periods, believing it could permanently secure the state.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise misreads 時詔 as "I ordered"; it is the office 侍詔.

proposals.before: In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother Chamberlain Zheng Ye as Marquis of Yangxin.
proposals.after: In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太后同母弟子 means son of the uterine younger brother; the literal omits 子 and makes Zheng Ye the brother himself.

decisions.reason: 元延四年 is Yuanyan year 4; with Yuanyan 1 = 12 BCE, year 4 is 9 BCE, so the parenthetical (12 BCE) is a conversion error and the proposed (9 BCE) is correct.
舅子滿 means a maternal uncle's son Man, not Ding Ming's son; the next unit names Man's father as Zhong (忠), so the before text invents a false filiation that the proposal correctly removes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封舅丁明為陽安侯，舅子滿為平周侯

decisions.reason: Chapter 時詔 is a corrupt writing of the office 待詔/侍詔 (Attendant-at-edict); Yan Shigu's text emends （時）〔待〕詔, and reading it as 'I commanded' invents imperial agency the Chinese does not support. The proposed office-title rendering is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: （時）〔待〕詔夏賀良等建言改元易號

decisions.reason: The literal's 'At the time I ordered' likewise misreads 時詔; critical editions restore 待詔 as Xia Heliang's office title, so Attendant-at-edict is the correct sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: （時）〔待〕詔夏賀良等建言改元易號，增益漏刻

decisions.reason: 太后同母弟子侍中鄭業 means Zheng Ye is the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother; the before literal drops 子 and wrongly makes Zheng Ye that brother himself.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太后同母弟子侍中鄭業為陽信侯
